title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: Post-war international cooperation framework
sections.summary: After World War II, great powers built a cooperative framework including the United Nations, World Bank and International Monetary Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Following the end of World War II, the great powers of the world came together to build a cooperative framework for international relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This included the setting up of the United Nations and the Bretton Woods institutions – namely the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.

sections.label: Russia's invasion of Ukraine
sections.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine breaches the rule of international law and directly challenges that rule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, Russia's invasion of Ukraine – in breach of this rule – is a direct challenge to the rule of international law itself.

sections.label: Israel-Hamas conflict escalation
sections.summary: The Israel-Hamas conflict has escalated dramatically since October, causing devastating loss of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Israel-Hamas conflict has escalated dramatically since October, resulting in devastating loss of life.

sections.label: Defence spending and Ministry priorities
sections.summary: The passage asks what the projections are for defence spending this year and the Ministry's priorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What are the projections for our defence spending this year and what are the Ministry's priorities?

sections.label: Ukrainian Armed Forces drone branch
sections.summary: Earlier this month, the Ukrainian President announced a separate branch of the Ukrainian Armed Forces devoted to drones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, the Ukrainian President announced the creation of a separate branch of the Ukrainian Armed Forces devoted to drones.

sections.label: SAF Next Generation transformation progress
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MINDEF can share the progress of the SAF's Next Generation transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: With all this going on, can MINDEF share on the progress of the SAF's Next Generation transformation plans?

sections.label: Defence investment and SAF capabilities
sections.summary: MINDEF previously informed the House that the SAF would add more platforms and capabilities over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We cannot wait until things are heating up to prioritise investing in defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, MINDEF previously informed the House that the SAF would be adding more platforms and capabilities over the next decade.

sections.label: F-35B aircraft purchases
sections.summary: MINDEF announced four F-35B aircraft in March 2019, later adding eight more for a total of twelve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In March 2019, MINDEF announced that it would purchase four F-35B aircraft, with an eye towards procuring a fleet of F-35s to replace the RSAF's ageing F-16 fleet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since then, MINDEF has announced that it would acquire an additional eight aircraft, for a total of twelve.

sections.label: Unmanned vehicles and RSN structure
sections.summary: The Minister for Defence said more unmanned aerial and ground vehicles would be introduced and half of RSN vessels would be unmanned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The Minister for Defence also said that more unmanned aerial and ground vehicles would be introduced in our combat units, and the RSN would be shifting towards a force structure, in which half of its vessels would be unmanned.

sections.label: Cost of one-way attack drones
sections.summary: One-way attack drones like those the Houthis use in the Red Sea are estimated to cost roughly US$2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One-way attack drones, like the ones that the Houthis are using in the Red Sea, are estimated to cost roughly US$2,000.

sections.label: US Marine Corps jet modification
sections.summary: A BBC report described the US Marine Corps modifying fighter jets for air defence against Houthi drone attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) report described how the United States (US) Marine Corps had modified its fighter jets to serve an air defence role, in response to Houthi drone attacks.

sections.label: MINDEF measures against evolving threats
sections.summary: The passage asks what MINDEF/SAF is doing against emerging technologies and tactics and how it trains personnel for evolving threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Given the rapidly changing security environment, what is MINDEF/SAF doing to safeguard against emerging and evolving technologies and tactics that can be used to undermine our security?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How is MINDEF training its personnel to meet evolving threats?

sections.label: Cyberattacks and MINDEF DIS response
sections.summary: Recalling past cyberattacks, it asks the Minister for Defence what MINDEF/SAF and the DIS are doing against digital threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Closer to home, we also remember the disruption caused by the SingHealth data breach in 2018, the distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on StarHub in 2016 and the 2017 cyberattack on MINDEF systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In view of Singapore's vulnerability to such attacks, could the Minister for Defence provide views on what MINDEF/SAF is doing to address threats in the digital domain, including steps that the Digital and Intelligence Service (DIS) is taking to guard against these threats?

sections.label: DIS progress update request
sections.summary: It asks whether MINDEF can provide a progress update on the Digital and Intelligence Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide a progress update on the DIS?

sections.label: Protecting undersea assets
sections.summary: Citing undersea attacks and damage, it asks the Minister for Defence to assure Singaporeans of ability to protect and repair undersea assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We know that these undersea assets can become targets for attack or sabotage during crisis and are also subject to accidental damage during peacetime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is evident from the 2022 Nord Stream 2 explosion, as well as the severing of submarine cables in the Baltic Sea and between Taiwan and Matsu last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Defence assure Singaporeans of our ability to protect and repair these undersea assets independently and in conjunction with partners?

sections.label: Israel-Hamas radicalisation risk
sections.summary: It states that a prolonged Israel-Hamas confrontation heightens radicalisation risk for Singapore and its neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Here, in Southeast Asia, a prolonged Israel-Hamas confrontation heightens the risk of radicalisation, posing a threat not just to Singapore but to our neighbours as well.

sections.label: Sophisticated ransomware groups
sections.summary: It states that ransomware groups are becoming more sophisticated, extracting data swiftly and using tailored threats to coerce victims into paying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Ransomware groups are becoming more sophisticated, swiftly extracting data and using tailored threats to coerce victims into paying up.

sections.label: ADMM ACICE establishment
sections.summary: It states Singapore established the ADMM ACICE in 2021 and that its physical centre launched on 18 July last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To address these challenges, Singapore took the proactive step of establishing the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Cybersecurity and Information Centre for Excellence, the ADMM ACICE, in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This move came amidst the growing digitalisation of society and the increasing prevalence of cyberattacks as well as disinformation and misinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am pleased that the physical centre for ACICE was officially launched on 18 July last year.

sections.label: ACICE cybersecurity disinformation work
sections.summary: The passage asks how ACICE intends to build on its existing work to enhance cybersecurity and combat disinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How does ACICE intend to build upon its existing work to enhance cybersecurity and combat disinformation?

sections.label: Ukraine, Middle East, US-China tensions
sections.summary: The passage notes the third year of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, risks of Middle East contagion, and a de facto US-China trade war.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Just last week was 24 February, another day in infamy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We are now in the third year of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: As many of the Members rightly pointed out, the Israel-Hamas conflict risks a contagion effect over the Middle East and there is a de facto trade war between the US and China.

sections.label: Russian gas share in Germany
sections.summary: The passage states that before the Ukraine invasion, Russia supplied 55% of gas consumed in Germany.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Before the Ukraine invasion, Russia supplied 55% of gas consumed in Germany.

sections.label: Hamas attack, Middle East, trade war
sections.summary: The passage states the US is striking the Houthis, the Saudis want peace, and the Hamas attack upended Middle East aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The US is striking the Houthis and the Saudis are saying: I want to make peace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: That attack by Hamas on 7 October 2023 upended, delayed, if not decimated, these aspirations in the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Between the US and China, a trade war has already started.

sections.label: Risk of regional global conflict
sections.summary: The passage states the risk of regional and even global conflict, even in the next decade, has become non-zero.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The risk of regional and even global conflict, even in the next decade, has become non-zero.

sections.label: Singapore self-defence, no backstop
sections.summary: The passage states a 30-member medical team was deployed and that Singapore cannot depend on another country to come to its rescue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We deployed a 30-member medical team to the region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But I want to make clear here, that if ever something similar happens to us here in Singapore, this Government, MINDEF and the SAF do not plan on the basis that we can depend on another country to come to our rescue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: If Singaporeans will not or cannot defend Singapore, there is no backstop.

sections.label: MINDEF projected defence expenditure
sections.summary: MINDEF projects about $20.2 billion in expenditure for the coming Financial Year, a 2.5% increase from FY23, while defence spending's share of GDP has been falling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the coming Financial Year, MINDEF projects an expenditure of around $20.2 billion – a 2.5% increase from last year, FY23.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Despite nominal increases for defence spending over the past years, the share as a percentage of GDP has been falling mainly because Singapore's GDP has been growing faster than defence spending.

sections.label: Defence spending two decades ago
sections.summary: Two decades ago, Singapore was spending 5% of GDP on defence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: As Members can see, two decades ago, we were spending 5% of GDP on defence.

sections.label: Future defence spending range
sections.summary: Defence spending can stay around 3% of GDP over the next decade, barring conflicts and wars, as total Government spending rose from 16% to 18% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Now, we could be decreasing because Total Government spending has been either maintained or is reducing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But total Government spending as a percentage of GDP has increased, from an average of 16% in the early 2000s to an average of 18% in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think if you listen to Deputy Prime Minister Wong, there are structural reasons why our economy and our revenue flows will not be as high as before.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I think it is good that we reach this level, and some of you have asked, including Mr Chong what are our future defence spending is, I would say that our spending can stay around 3%, move up or down a bit, but in this range over the next decade, with one important caveat: barring conflicts and wars, obviously.

sections.label: F-35 aircraft orders
sections.summary: An order is being placed to acquire eight F-35As, adding to the 12 F-35Bs already ordered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have ordered, as Ms Poh Li San said four plus eight F-35Bs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This time, we are putting in an order to acquire eight F-35As, adding to our 12 F-35Bs.

sections.label: F-16 drawdown and F-35B delivery
sections.summary: The F-16s will be drawn down progressively from mid-2030 onwards, and the first four F-35Bs ordered four years ago will be received in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The F-16s, after their mid-life upgrade, will be drawn down progressively from mid-2030 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We will receive the first four F-35Bs which we ordered four years ago in 2026; it seems to be on schedule.

sections.label: F-35A arrival around 2030
sections.summary: The F-35A variant announced today will arrive around 2030 if Parliament approves this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The F-35A variant that I am announcing today, if Parliament approves this Budget, will arrive around 2030.

sections.label: RSAF fleet after F-16s
sections.summary: After the F-16s retire, the RSAF will operate F-35As, F-35Bs and F-15SGs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In sum, after the F-16s retire, the RSAF will operate F-35As, F-35Bs and F15SGs.

sections.label: Four submarines operational by 2028
sections.summary: Defence spending is long-term, and all four submarines will be operational around Singapore waters by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Defence spending is a long-term business and because we stuck to it, all four submarines will be operational around Singapore waters by 2028.

sections.label: New Howitzers capabilities
sections.summary: The new Howitzers are self-loading, shoot faster and move, and require 60% less manpower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The new Howitzers are self-loading, shoot faster and move, and require 60% less manpower.

sections.label: Navy Unmanned Surface Vessel operational
sections.summary: This year, the Navy's Unmanned Surface Vessel goes fully operational.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And it is a given in any modern military, and it will be increasingly used, and we will do the same.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, this year, the Navy's Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) goes fully operational.

sections.label: Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise
sections.summary: The DIS co-organised the Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise in November last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The DIS co-organised the Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise (CIDeX) in November last year.

sections.label: Digital range completion 2026
sections.summary: A digital range replicates these systems and will be completed in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But we have a digital range that replicates these systems.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: That digital range will be completed in 2026.

sections.label: Expanded Shoalwater Bay training
sections.summary: Singapore deployed 4,300 personnel and 450 platforms to Shoalwater Bay, and this year's expanded area will increase exercise scale by close to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Last year, we deployed 4,300 personnel, 450 platforms to Shoalwater Bay.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, not only is Singapore committed to its defence, we have friends who are willing to open up their country to allow us to put all these platforms there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And this year, the expanded training area will allow us to increase the scale of exercise by close to 50%, with an increase in training duration for six to nine weeks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The SAF will have a combined training area 10 times the size of Singapore.

sections.label: Phase 1 opening 2025
sections.summary: Phase 1 will be opening from 2025, and Senior Minister of State Heng will speak on this in more detail.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In the picture that you see, Phase 1 will be opening from 2025, and Senior Minister of State Heng will speak on this in more detail.

sections.label: Manpower reduction and civilian skills
sections.summary: Dr Ng Eng Hen told the House to expect a one-third manpower reduction by 2030, and the SAF can tap civilian know-how.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In fact, Minister for Defence Dr Ng Eng Hen, has told this House that we are to expect a one-third reduction in manpower by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Needless to say, this will have profound implications to the way we organise the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF).

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As the Russia-Ukraine conflict has clearly demonstrated, the competence and digital savviness of a civilian population that dons the military uniform in times of war, can be a decisive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Indeed, there is much more the SAF can do to tap on our people's civilian know-how to strengthen our capabilities.

sections.label: Functional assessments for pre-enlistees
sections.summary: MINDEF pivoted from combat fit and non-combat fit classification to functional assessments, with 75 of 100 pre-enlistees deployable to wider roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On the other hand, Russian cyber-attacks on government systems and critical infrastructure augmented its ground invasion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It was therefore timely that MINDEF pivoted away from the dichotomous classification of pre-enlistees into "combat fit" and "non-combat fit" groups, to implementing functional assessments two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How updated at last year's Committee of Supply (COS) that out of the 100 pre-enlistees with orthopaedic conditions who underwent the relevant functional assessments, 75 were deployable to a wider range of operational roles than before.

sections.label: Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme
sections.summary: The Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme deploys NSmen to roles aligned to their school or workplace expertise, creating a win-win situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: MINDEF previously announced that it had sought to maximise the contributions of NSmen through the Enhanced Expertise Deployment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By deploying NSmen to roles that are aligned to the expertise that they have acquired in school or in their workplaces, a win-win situation is thus created.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This not only enhances the SAF's operational capabilities and addresses their manpower needs, but also provides NSmen with the opportunity to practise their specialised skills in a military setting.

sections.label: Enterprise Safety Information System update
sections.summary: MINDEF provided an update on implementing the enterprise Safety Information System, facilitating rank and file reporting on near misses and incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Last year, MINDEF provided an update on the implementation of the enterprise Safety Information System, facilitating rank and file reporting on near misses and incidents.

sections.label: SAF Enterprise Safety Information System
sections.summary: ESIS marks a milestone in digital, data-driven safety management, offering situational awareness, predictive analytics and accident prevention to revolutionise SAF safety protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Notably, the SAF's Enterprise Safety Information System (ESIS) marks a significant milestone in leveraging digital technologies and data-driven safety management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By facilitating enhanced situational awareness, predictive analytics and accident prevention mechanisms, ESIS promises to revolutionise the safety protocols within the SAF.

sections.label: US Army Global Assessment Tool
sections.summary: The US Army developed the Global Assessment Tool to measure soldiers' psychosocial well-being in emotional, social, family and spiritual fitness domains.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With this in mind, the United States (US) Army developed the Global Assessment Tool (GAT) to measure psychosocial well-being of their soldiers in the domains of emotional, social, family and spiritual fitness.

sections.label: US Army Master Resilience Training
sections.summary: The US Army has a 10-day Master Resilience Training Programme covering self-awareness, self-regulation, optimism, mental agility, strength of character and connection.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To bolster this, the US Army also has a 10-day Master Resilience Training Programme in the core competencies of self-awareness, self-regulation, optimism, mental agility, strength of character and connection.

sections.label: Digitising NS administrative processes
sections.summary: MINDEF unveiled OneNS and an automated make-up pay claim system, and is asked what further steps digitise administrative processes for NSmen and employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply debate last year, MINDEF unveiled the OneNS platform and also highlighted the introduction of an automated system to calculate make-up pay claim amounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As the filing of make-up pay and claims has been a major administrative burden for many employers and NSmen, could MINDEF share the additional steps taken to digitise and improve administrative processes for our NSmen?

sections.label: OneNS app replacing NS Portal
sections.summary: MINDEF is asked when the OneNS app will officially replace the NS Portal and whether further improvements followed earlier trial roll-outs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF provide an update of when the OneNS app will officially replace the NS Portal platform, and whether further improvements have been made following earlier trial roll-outs?

sections.label: Centralised NS services hub
sections.summary: In 2019, plans were announced for a centralised hub consolidating all NS-related services into one location to better cater to NSmen's needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2019, plans were announced for a centralised hub that would consolidate all NS-related services into one location to better cater to the needs of our NSmen.

sections.label: NS salary and Local Qualifying Salary
sections.summary: The median NS salary should be at least the Local Qualifying Salary of $1,600 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The median NS salary should be at least the Local Qualifying Salary of $1,600 a month.

sections.label: IPS study on NS skills
sections.summary: A 2023 IPS study found 29% of over 1,000 surveyed Singaporeans felt NSF could not learn useful civilian employment skills through NS, higher than 18% ten years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2023 IPS study found that 29% of the over 1,000 Singaporans surveyed did not feel that NSF could learn skills that were useful for civilian employment through NS.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This 29% is higher than the 18% recorded 10 years ago.

sections.label: Questions on SkillsFuture@NS and post-NS transition
sections.summary: Questions ask MINDEF for updates on SkillsFuture@NS initiatives, plans for NSFs' post-NS transition including entrepreneurs and freelancers, and improving perceptions of NS value to employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, can MINDEF provide an update on the SkillsFture@NS initiatives that were launched in 2022, including SkillsFuture@NS Learning eXperience Platform?

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, what are MINDEF's plans to facilitate NSFs' transition post-NS, including those who aspire to become entrepreneurs or who must prepare to freelance if they join the creative, media, and coaching sectors?

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, what are MINDEF's plans to improve perceptions of the value of NS to soldiers' employability?

sections.label: Launch of Exercise SG Ready
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong recently launched the inaugural Total Defence Exercise, Exercise SG Ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong recently launched the inaugural Total Defence Exercise – Exercise SG Ready.

sections.label: NSmen cash credit and recognition packages
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced a special cash credit for former and current NSmen in Budget 2024, alongside initiatives like the NS55 Recognition Package and enhanced NS HOME Awards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced a special cash credit for former and current NSmen in Budget 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In recent years, I have been heartened to see initiatives like the NS55 Recognition Package and the enhancement of the NS HOME Awards.

sections.label: 40th anniversary of Total Defence
sections.summary: The 40th anniversary of Total Defence this year is an ideal opportunity for the community to contemplate how each can contribute to Singapore's defence.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: As we commemorate the 40th anniversary of Total Defence this year, it presents an ideal opportunity for us, as a community, to come together and contemplate how each of us can contribute to Singapore's defence.

sections.label: Proliferation of hybrid threats
sections.summary: The passage states that beyond armed conflicts, hybrid threats such as dis- and misinformation and coordinated influence campaigns have proliferated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Aside from armed conflicts, we have seen the proliferation of hybrid threats – from the likes of dis- and misinformation to well-coordinated online and offline influence campaigns.

sections.label: RSN inclusive workspace update
sections.summary: The passage seeks an update from MINDEF on steps taken to make RSN naval vessels a more inclusive and open workspace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I would like to seek an update from MINDEF on the steps and measures taken thus far in making RSN's naval vessels a more inclusive and open workspace that is fair and just to all Singaporean servicepersons.

sections.label: Strengthening total defence understanding
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MINDEF can do more to strengthen Singaporeans' understanding of total defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF do more to strengthen the understanding of total defence among Singaporeans?

sections.label: ACCORD support for NS transition
sections.summary: The passage asks whether ACCORD has considered steps to support those transitioning out of full-time NS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Has ACCORD also considered steps to support those transitioning out of full-time NS?

sections.label: NS awareness and re-imagining
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on raising community awareness of NS and the SAF, and whether NS can be re-imagined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can MINDEF provide an update on its plans to raise community awareness about the importance of NS and of a strong SAF?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In light of our evolving threat environment, can we re-imagine NS to go beyond its current form, scope and method?

sections.label: Deployment beyond medical classifications
sections.summary: The passage states that about 200 of 280 pre-enlistees tested since 2022 were deployed, allowing more deployment options than medical classifications alone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This allows for more deployment options than if one were to rely purely on medical classifications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We were able to deploy about 200 out of the 280 pre-enlistees tested since 2022 to contribute effectively in the wider range of roles.

sections.label: SAF role redesign for NSFs
sections.summary: Since 2021 the SAF redesigned 1,800 roles in vocations, letting about 700 NSFs take on operational roles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since 2021, the SAF has redesigned 1,800 roles in vocations, such as Combat Medics, Infantry Carrier Vehicle Operators and Transport Operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This has allowed about 700 NSFs to take on important operational roles, compared to if the roles were not redesigned.

sections.label: Work-Learn Schemes enrolment
sections.summary: There are now eight Work-Learn Schemes with about 520 NSFs enrolled since 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: With this, we have now eight Work-Learn Schemes with about 520 NSFs enrolled since 2018.

sections.label: NSmen redeployment into roles
sections.summary: About 790 NSmen have been redeployed over the years into roles such as C4 operators and legal officers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In total, about 790 NSmen have been redeployed over the years into roles, such as Command, Control, Communications and Computers (C4) operators and legal officers.

sections.label: Inspector-General's Office audit cycle
sections.summary: The Inspector-General's Office commenced its third audit cycle in April 2023, covering formations across the Services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Inspector-General's Office commenced its third audit cycle in April 2023, covering formations across the Services.

sections.label: SAF mental health support
sections.summary: An anonymous 24-hour SAF counselling hotline exists, full-time mental health professionals doubled to 80, and a Mental Health Office was established.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Those who are uncomfortable sharing their problems openly can call an anonymous 24-hour SAF counselling hotline.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We have also doubled the number of full-time mental health professionals to 80 over the past decade and established a Mental Health Office for better synergy and delivery of care.

sections.label: NS Portal and OneNS
sections.summary: NSmen use the NS Portal for major transactions, and this year it will be replaced by a new OneNS web portal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Today, NSmen use the NS Portal for their major NS-related transactions, such as to apply for Exit Permits, to book Individual Physical Proficiency Tests (IPPT), and to receive and acknowledge NS notices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This year, the NS Portal will be replaced by a new OneNS web portal.

sections.label: NS app attendance registration
sections.summary: NSmen can register attendance using the app's geo-location and QR code scanning features, rolled out to all NS units in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: With this enhancement, they will be able to register their attendance easily with the app's geo-location and QR code scanning features.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This will be rolled out to all NS units in 2024.

sections.label: New CMPB opening
sections.summary: The new Central Manpower Base will open in phases from 2025, as the Defence Minister spoke about last evening.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As the Defence Minister spoke about last evening when he made his speech, the new Central Manpower Base (CMPB) will be open in phases from the year 2025.

sections.label: More RHHs and sports centre
sections.summary: SAF will establish up to four more RHHs over the next decade, with the third at Dieppe Barracks housing a Sports and Exercise Medicine Centre from 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Over the next decade, the SAF will be establishing up to four more RHHs in different parts of the island.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The third RHH will be located at the Dieppe Barracks to serve the north.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It will house the SAF's first Sports and Exercise Medicine Centre, to better manage musculoskeletal injuries and that is slated to commence operations in 2027.

sections.label: NS HOME Awards enhancement
sections.summary: After the NS HOME Awards were enhanced again in 2022, an NSman can receive up to $18,500 over his NS journey.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: After we enhanced the NS HOME Awards again in 2022, a NSman can receive up to $18,500 in the course of his NS journey.

sections.label: LifeSG credits for NSmen
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced all past and present NSmen will receive $200 in LifeSG credits in November this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Most recently, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced that all past and present NSmen will receive $200 in LifeSG credits in November this year.

sections.label: NS allowance reviews
sections.summary: The allowance is regularly reviewed, most recently in July 2023, and was reviewed four times from 2012 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And this allowance is regularly reviewed, most recently in July 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And I must also say that if you look over 10 years since 2012, from 2012 to 2023, this allowance was reviewed four times.

sections.label: SkillsFuture@NS and Career Starter Lab
sections.summary: MINDEF and MHA partnered NTUC to enhance SkillsFuture@NS, giving NSFs access to 75,000 online courses, and launched the Career Starter Lab programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In 2022, MINDEF and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) partnered the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Learning Hub and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) to enhance the SkillsFuture@NS initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Under this enhancement, NSFs can use the SkillsFuture@NS Learning eXperience Platform to gain unlimited access to 75,000 online courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Since its implementation, about 21,000 NSFs have signed up on the platform.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: MINDEF/SAF and Young NTUC also launched the Career Starter Lab programme to NSFs in September 2023, to support them with structured job training and career mentorship after NS.

sections.label: NS Square redevelopment
sections.summary: The Float@Marina Bay's redevelopment into the NS Square is on track, with construction commencing next month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Float@Marina Bay's redevelopment into the NS Square is on track, with construction commencing next month.

sections.label: Total Defence 40th anniversary
sections.summary: This year marks the 40th anniversary of Total Defence, which since 1984 has been Singapore's overarching defence strategy and whole-of-society response.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I will address how we are building commitment to Singapore and strengthening resilience through Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year marks the 40th anniversary of Total Defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 1984, Total Defence has been our overarching defence strategy and a whole-of-society response against any threat to our sovereignty, our security and our way of life.

sections.label: Digital Defence pillar
sections.summary: Campaigns can sow distrust, increase anxiety and create divisions if communities are not united and vigilant, which is why Digital Defence was stood up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Such campaigns can sow distrust, increase anxiety and create divisions within communities if we are not united and vigilant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This is why we stood up our newest pillar of Digital Defence.

sections.label: TD40 campaign and Exercise SG Ready
sections.summary: A year-long campaign commemorates 40 years of Total Defence, and organisations participated in the inaugural island-wide Exercise SG Ready.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about how we are commemorating 40 years of Total Defence (TD40).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We have planned a year-long campaign to raise Singapore's threat awareness, as well as strengthen our resilience and readiness for crises and disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over the past two weeks, education, community, commercial and Government organisations have participated in the inaugural island-wide Total Defence exercise, called Exercise SG Ready.

sections.label: Exercise SG Ready participation
sections.summary: More than 800 participating organisations have come on board and simulated some 250 power, 300 water or food supply, and 200 cyber disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We launched the exercise about two weeks ago, and as Mr Chong Kee Hiong noted, we had 500 participating organisations then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But two weeks on today, more than 800 participating organisations have come on board and simulated some 250 power disruptions, 300 water or food supply disruptions, and 200 cyber disruptions.

sections.label: Civil Defence shelter visits
sections.summary: About 12,000 people visited Civil Defence shelters at three MRT stations, and over 160 businesses enhanced their business continuity plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Last week, about 12,000 members of the public visited Civil Defence shelters at three MRT stations where they learnt shelter procedures and about how these shelters protect civilians in an emergency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Over 160 businesses took the opportunity to enhance and validate their business continuity plans.

sections.label: Total Defence Convention April
sections.summary: MINDEF and NUS will jointly organise a Total Defence Convention for partners and practitioners in April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MINDEF and NUS will jointly organise a Total Defence Convention for our partners and practitioners in April.

sections.label: The Sandbox and TD@Singverse
sections.summary: The Sandbox is in its third year, more proposals were shortlisted, and over 3,500 players joined the TD@Singverse virtual world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The Sandbox is now in its third year, and I am happy to update that we continue to receive many ideas, especially from our youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This year, we have shortlisted more proposals for implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since its launch a week ago, over 3,500 players have joined the TD@Singverse virtual world where they have learnt about the six pillars of Total Defence through mini games.

sections.label: IPS survey on NS attitudes
sections.summary: An IPS survey found 98% of respondents agreed NS was necessary, and close to 90% would encourage others to serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: According to an Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) survey on Public Attitudes towards NS, concluded last year, 98% of respondents agreed that NS was necessary in the defence of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Close to 90% would encourage their friends and loved ones to serve NS even if NS was not compulsory.

sections.label: ACCORD signs MOUs
sections.summary: Last year, ACCORD signed Memoranda of Understanding with AETOS and Singapore Human Resource Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Last year, ACCORD signed Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with AETOS and Singapore Human Resource Institute.

sections.label: Women in SAF Volunteer Corps
sections.summary: Since 2015, more than 600 women have volunteered in the SAF Volunteer Corps and been trained and deployed in various roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since 2015, more than 600 women have volunteered as part of our SAF Volunteer Corps and have been trained and deployed in roles such as in surveillance operations, engineering and safety.

sections.label: NS enlistment and basic upkeep
sections.summary: Enlisting young male citizens into NS calls on their time for two years, or 22 months with a certain fitness level, and they need basic upkeep during this duty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: And when we enlist our young male citizens into NS, we do not just take them in as volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
sentences.text: We recognise that we call on their time for two years – well, 22 months if they have a certain level of fitness – and that during this period they do need basic upkeep as they fulfil their duty to this country.

sections.label: Halal kitchen on naval ships
sections.summary: For these reasons, a separate halal kitchen on our naval ships is not feasible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For these reasons, a separate halal kitchen on our naval ships is not feasible.

sections.label: Exercise SG Ready participation
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Zaqy shared Exercise SG Ready, with more than 800 organisations taking part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In my cut on Total Defence, I had asked about how the whole-of-nation is getting itself ready as well and I think Senior Minister of State Zaqy shared exercise SG Ready on this – which was very heartening, more than 800 organisations taking part.

sections.label: Total Defence year-long initiatives
sections.summary: Initiatives will run the whole year long, with plans including the Total Defence Exhibition, TD Sandbox, Dynamic Defence Display and Total Defence Awards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As I shared earlier on, our initiatives will run the whole year long and we hope that beyond this, we can expand this and certainly get more onboard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If you look at some of the events that we are planning – not just the TD Exercise – we got the Total Defence Exhibition; we have the TD Sandbox that is ongoing with the schools for our youths; we got the Dynamic Defence Display; as well as the Total Defence Awards.
